newsitem.title: CANADA: NorTel says Q4 order input up 41 percent.
newsitem.headline: NorTel says Q4 order input up 41 percent.

text.p: Northern Telecom Ltd said on Monday its order input for the fourth quarter of 1996 was a record US$5.27 billion, up 41 percent from US$3.74 billion recorded in the same period last year.
Order input for 1996 was US$14.08 billion, versus US$10.99 billion in 1995, the company said.

North American sales were significantly higher than in 1995 in the quarter. The company said that international sales grew over 1995 in the period, with "substantial" gains in Europe and growth in Asia Pacific partially offset by a "substantial" decline in the Caribbean and Latin America.

"For the year, all geographic regions grew compared to 1995, underpinned by the substantial gains in the United States and significant growth in Europe and Asia Pacific, with more modest gains from Canada and CALA," NorTel said.
The telecommunications equipment maker said wireless and broadband networks sales both rose in the quarter.

"Enterprise networks revenues grew sharply, with significant growth experienced in the United States and Europe and strong growth across all other geographic areas. In the quarter compared to the same period last year, switching networks revenues declined slightly," NorTel said.

In 1996, sales from network businesses rose over 1995 with wireless and broadband Networks posting "substantial" increases. Fourth quarter sales overall were US$4.19 billion, a 20 percent increase from US$3.50 billion reported for the same period in 1995. Sales also rose 20 percent in the year, to US$12.85 billion from US$10.67 billion in 1995.

Selling, general and administrative costs were US$685 million, or 16.4 percent of sales, in the quarter, versus with US$549 million, or 15.7 percent, in the 1995 period. For the year, SG&A expenses were US$2.20 billion, or 17.1 percent of revenues, versus US$1.92 billion, or 18.0 percent, in 1995.

Fourth quarter research and development costs rose to US$526 million, or 12.5 percent of sales, as compared with US$449 million, or 12.8 percent, for 1995 quarter. For 1996, R&D expenses climbed to US$1.81 billion, or 14.1 percent of revenues, from US$1.58 billion, or 14.8 percent, in 1995.

"We are pleased with the order, revenue and earnings growth achieved in 1996 and especially pleased with our order backlog of US$6 billion at the end of 1996," NorTel president and chief executive Jean Monty said in a statement.
